items.title: MemDreamer: Decoupling Perception and Reasoning for Long Video Understanding via Hierarchical Graph Memory and Agentic Retrieval Mechanism
items.title_zh: MemDreamer：通过分层图记忆与 Agent 检索机制解耦长视频理解的感知与推理
items.summary: MemDreamer streams long videos into a three-tier Hierarchical Graph Memory anchored by a foundational graph of spatiotemporal and causal relations, then lets a reasoning model navigate it through an Observation-Reason-Action retrieval loop with tool augmentation. It reports state-of-the-art results on four benchmarks, narrowing the gap to human experts to 3.7 points while constraining the reasoning context to 2% of full-context ingestion and gaining 12.5 points absolute accuracy.

items.title: Beyond English benchmarks: clinical llm evaluation in Brazilian Portuguese
items.title_zh: 超越英语基准：巴西葡萄牙语临床 LLM 评估
items.summary: ClinicalBr is a bilingual Portuguese-English benchmark built from 2,892 Brazilian clinical case reports across 28 SciELO medical journals and 18 specialties, supporting diagnosis retrieval, differential diagnosis, exam recommendation and treatment planning. Evaluating MedGemma-27B, Sabiá-4, DeepSeek-R1 and o3-mini, the authors find the Portuguese-English gap is task-dependent: English leads by 7.5-12.1 accuracy points on diagnosis retrieval, but the advantage disappears on the other tasks.

items.title: Act As a Real Researcher: A Suite of Benchmarks Evaluating Frontier LLMs and Agentic Harnesses in Research Lifecycle
items.title_zh: 像真正的研究者一样行动：评估前沿 LLM 与 Agent 框架在研究生命周期中表现的基准套件
items.summary: AARRI-Bench is the first benchmark in the AARR series, testing whether agents emulate the professionalism, thoroughness and nuanced reasoning of human researchers in granular research scenarios rather than only macro-level execution. Across frontier models and agentic harnesses the best configuration, Mini-SWE-Agent with Claude Opus 4.7, reached only 68.3% success, frequently overlooking details obvious to real human researchers.

items.title: Cherry-pick Override: LLM Judges Under-use the Non-Directional Verdicts Their Contract Authorizes
items.title_zh: Cherry-pick Override：LLM 评审未充分利用其契约授权的非方向性裁决
items.summary: The paper defines directional overcommitment, where an LLM judge returns Supports or Refutes on a claim whose contract authorizes a non-directional verdict such as Conflicting or Not Enough Evidence. On AVeriTeC's gold-Conflicting subset a four-option typed panel committed directionally on 18.7% of claims and four frozen judges on 21.3-48.0%; asked in a fresh context, two judges identified the conflict on about two thirds of their own CPO claims, versus under 0.12 for claims they had committed correctly.

items.title: How reliable are LLMs when it comes to playing dice?
items.summary: The authors benchmark eight state-of-the-art models on standard and counterintuitive discrete-probability problems, with and without chain-of-thought prompting. Average accuracy was 0.96 on standard problems but 0.59 on counterintuitive ones; performance dropped by over 20% when canonical formulations were disguised and by up to 34% with misleading suggestions embedded in the prompt, with no model immune.

items.title: Unsupervised Continual Clustering via Forward-Backward Knowledge Distillation
items.title_zh: 通过前向-后向知识蒸馏的无监督持续聚类
items.summary: The authors introduce Unsupervised Continual Clustering and propose FBCC, which uses a continual teacher network with a clustering projector plus lightweight task-specific students in a dual-phase forward-backward distillation process. Across four benchmark datasets it improves clustering accuracy over continual-learning baselines while reducing catastrophic forgetting without storing past data.

items.title: VisualFLIP: Do Predictions Depend on Task-Critical Visual Evidence in Multimodal Reasoning?
items.title_zh: VisualFLIP：多模态推理的预测是否依赖任务关键视觉证据？
items.summary: VisualFLIP is a paired benchmark of 1,374 images organized as same-question perturbation pairs across cardinality, attribute, spatial and logic tasks, used to evaluate 24 multimodal models on whether their correct answers actually depend on task-critical visual evidence.
